title: fix(types,plugin-detail): the authoring mirror declares `add.picker.filter` as the contract's rule array (objectui#9964)
body:
Fixes #9964

objectui's authoring mirror typed `record:related_list` `add.picker.filter` as `unknown` while the component that consumes it types the same key as `ViewFilterRule[]`, and four `(schema as any).add` reads in `record-related-list.tsx` kept the divergence invisible. The mirror now carries the contract's rule array, all four casts are gone, and a compile-rejection pin goes red when either half is put back.

Clause-②: no

Re-derived from this branch's own diff, not copied: the only declared type this change moves is `RecordRelatedListComponentProps.add.picker.filter`, from `unknown` to the contract's rule array. No key is added, removed or renamed; no runtime value changes; the renderer edits delete casts and nothing else. That is a narrowing being UNDONE rather than an authoring surface being narrowed — the protocol never accepted anything but the array here, and refuses the rest at parse today (measured below, both directions). A value that a TypeScript consumer can no longer assign is a value the publish call it was heading for already refused.

## The spec reading, re-taken in this act

**Source**, `/home/user/objectstack` at `04d639c659`, cited by symbol rather than by line address (AGENTS.md #11):

- `RecordRelatedListProps` is a `strictObject`; its `add` member is a `strictObject`; that block's `picker` member is a `strictObject`; and inside it the `filter` member is declared `z.array(ViewFilterRuleSchema).optional()`, described as "Restrict which records the picker offers."

**Installed artifact**, the `@objectstack/spec` this workspace resolves (17.4.0) — the one both declarations actually mirror, read at runtime so the source reading cannot be the only leg:

```
add keys:    picker,linkField,label
picker keys: object,valueField,labelField,filter
filter:      optional -> array
parse [{field,operator,value}] -> success: true
parse {active: true}           -> success: false
parse 'active = true'          -> success: false
```

Both readings agree, so the dispatch's condition for stopping does not hold: the contract DOES declare the array form. The component agrees with the protocol; the mirror was the side that disagreed, by being looser than the contract it mirrors. **The mirror moves, the consumer's guard stays** — AGENTS.md #0.1, fix the producer, never accrete a lenient renderer-side dialect.

## What changed

1. **The mirror** — `packages/types/src/record-components.ts`. `filter?: unknown` becomes `filter?: ViewFilterRule[]`, with `ViewFilterRule` added to the `@objectstack/spec/ui` type import that file already carried for `I18nLabel`. **The spelling was not invented**: `ViewFilterRule` is the spec's own exported type, it is what `@object-ui/types` re-exports under that exact name from its index, and it is the spelling every other filter-rule array in this repo uses (`app-shell`'s `viewFilterFold` and `ObjectDataPage`, and `RelatedList`'s own prop). A local rule-array alias would have been a second declaration of the same thing, which is the defect this card is about.

2. **All four casts** — `packages/plugin-detail/src/renderers/record-related-list.tsx`. The condition, the spread, the `pickLocalized` label read and the `onRowDelete` fallback now read `schema.add`. **No second divergence surfaced**: with the mirror fixed, `tsc --noEmit` on this package exits 0, and the ablation below shows that with the mirror put back the un-cast reads produce exactly one error in the whole package — the known TS2322 on `picker.filter`, no second one behind it.

3. **The pins.** A new compile-rejection pin in `@object-ui/types`, and the objectui#9475 guard next door had its ledger emptied — that guard listed the `add` cast as load-bearing and asserted it STILL PRESENT, so it is what went red when the casts were removed. That is the mechanism working: the exemption could not outlive its subject. With the ledger empty, its derived "no cast stands between `schema` and any contract-declared key" guard now covers `add` with no carve-out.

## The pin, and why it is not a render test

A runtime test cannot see this defect at all: `unknown` and `ViewFilterRule[]` are the same zero bytes, the picker receives the same value, and every behavioural assertion is green on the defect and on the fix alike. So the pin reads a compiler, in the two shapes this repo already uses:

- **type-level legs** compiled by `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json` and erased by vitest, in the idiom `record-related-list.relationshipValueFieldUncast-9475.test.tsx` uses next door: an invariant type-equality assertion, direction proofs that make a broken instrument red rather than green, and a `@ts-expect-error` pinned to the PRE-FIX shape so the directive goes unused (TS2578) if the mirror returns to `unknown`. The expected shape is DERIVED from the spec's own schema in the same file, not restated (AGENTS.md #9);
- **diagnostic legs** that compile authored snippets against the mirror SOURCE through the TypeScript API and read the diagnostics back, so the same property also fails under vitest — the idiom of `core`'s `freeze-schema.types.test.ts` and `scripts/__tests__/js-comment-mask-param-types-9324.test.ts`. Three wrong shapes must be refused, the canonical authored array must still be accepted (without that half, "the wrong shapes error" is also satisfied by a face too narrow to use), and two controls on a member this card never touched stay identical on both legs.

The file carries its own discrimination: every case is compiled a SECOND time against the pre-fix declaration, and `EXPECTED_FLIPS` names which four that reverts.

## Gates

Every exit code was captured to a file and read back, never through a pipe.

| gate | exit | reading |

| `@object-ui/types` `tsc --noEmit` | 0 | |
| `@object-ui/types` `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json` | 0 | the leg that reads the type-level pins |
| `@object-ui/plugin-detail` `tsc --noEmit` | 0 | the un-cast reads, against the rebuilt mirror |
| `@object-ui/plugin-detail` `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json` | 0 | |
| `vitest run packages/types/ packages/plugin-detail/` (under the lock) | 0 | 408 files, 6890 tests passed |
| `eslint` on the 5 changed files | 0 | 5 files linted, 0 errors, 34 warnings, all pre-existing `no-explicit-any` plus the pin's deliberate `any` direction proof |
| `check:control-bytes` | 0 | 8197 tracked text files |

| `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` | 0 | `minor` + `patch`, never `major` |
| `check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test` (5 paths) | 0 | NOT GOVERNED — none of the 5 governed surfaces matched |

**Declared narrowing.** `eslint` ran on the five changed files, not repo-wide. The population it was narrowed from is what `eslint .` enumerates from `eslint.config.js`; CI owns that run. The narrowing cannot hide a verdict this diff moved: **type-aware linting is not enabled in this repo** — `eslint.config.js` configures no `parserOptions.project` and no `projectService`, so every rule judges one file's syntax in isolation and a type declaration change is invisible to the verdict on any file this diff does not edit. The count is `--format json`'s own: 5 files.

`vitest` ran the two affected packages rather than the whole tree, which is this repo's documented path-filtered form from the repo root; the full suite is CI's.

## Ablation

Direction predicted in writing before each leg ran. Both legs mutated on disk through a refuse-on-zero-match tool with an anchor declared to hit exactly once, verified in both directions by blob hash, and restored under a trap with `git checkout HEAD -- ABSOLUTE_PATH`; each restore is proven by `git diff HEAD` empty AND the blob equal to the HEAD blob.

**Leg A — ⭐ the one that matters: put the mirror back to `unknown`** (anchor x1, blob `7607d283c1d7` to `326336b9e70a`, restored to `7607d283c1d7`).

| measurement | predicted | observed |
|---|---|---|
| the new pin under vitest | RED | RED — 6 failed / 4 passed: the four diagnostic cases plus both discrimination assertions |
| `@object-ui/types` `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json` | RED | RED — exit 2, two TS2344 (the equality legs) and one TS2578 (the pre-fix `@ts-expect-error` went unused) |
| `@object-ui/plugin-detail` `tsc --noEmit`, after rebuilding the mirror's `dist` | RED, exactly one TS2322 | RED — exit 2, **one** error in the whole package, TS2322 at the un-cast `add` prop: "The types of 'picker.filter' are incompatible between these types. Type 'unknown' is not assignable to type ... array". This reproduces the card's headline measurement independently |

The mirror's `dist` was rebuilt again after the restore and re-read, so the tree carries no leftover of the mutation.

**Leg B — reinstate ONE of the four casts** (anchor x1, blob `52445e1e1163` to `53fe495ef6c4`, restored to `52445e1e1163`).

| measurement | predicted | observed |
|---|---|---|
| the objectui#9475 guard under vitest | RED | RED — 2 failed: the derived "no cast over any contract-declared key" leg and the new un-cast leg |
| `@object-ui/plugin-detail` `tsc --noEmit` | GREEN | GREEN — exit 0, no output |

Leg B's second row is the point of having both pins: a cast is always type-legal, so the compiler cannot see one creep back, and the source-text guard cannot see the mirror loosen. Either pin alone leaves one half of this card unprotected.

## The ledger entry, and why it is in this diff

`check:spec-symbols` went red on this branch and its own remedy text says why: `CLAIM_DEBT` in `scripts/check-spec-symbol-derivation.mjs` listed `RecordRelatedListComponentProps` as a symbol whose "aligned with the spec" claim had nothing structural behind it. The first of the three exits that ledger's header prescribes is "make the claim structural (derive from / import the spec type) — the claim becomes structural and the entry goes", and that is exactly what tightening the mirror did. The entry is deleted; the deletion was checked against `--claim-ledger`'s regenerated block, which differs from the committed one by that one line and nothing else. The gate then exits 0, and the eight `scripts/__tests__` suites that read this script pass. This removes an exemption rather than adding one.

## `check:changeset-claims` — the read it asked for

The gate is report-only and names two pending changesets whose bodies mention a file this change edits. It judges name resolution, never meaning, so the question is mine to answer; I read both paragraphs, and neither claim is falsified:

- `8649-detail-renderer-undeclared-keys.md` — it describes the annotation-erasing destructure default being removed from three renderers. That default is untouched here: this renderer still binds `schema` with the annotation-preserving spelling objectui#8649 installed, and the claim's closing "No published surface moves" is a statement about that change, not this one.
- `9280-record-highlights-entry-icon-retired.md` — it describes `RecordHighlightsComponentProps.fields[]`, a different interface that happens to live in the same file. This change does not touch it.

## Acceptance notes

- **Out of scope, noted and not filed as part of this PR:** the same interface's TOP-LEVEL `filter` is declared `any` while the contract declares it the same rule array. It is the same class as this card but NOT a mechanical copy of this repair, and it is deliberately left alone: `RelatedList`'s own `filter` prop is declared as the rule array OR a composed ObjectQL node, because `ElementDataSourceGate` writes the composed component-AND-view-AND-binding filter onto that key at runtime; and an existing fixture in `p1-spec-alignment.test.ts` annotates a triple-array against it. Which of the two shapes the authoring face should carry is a contract question, not a cleanup, so it is reported to the dispatching seat with dedupe words rather than widened into this card.
- Everything else in the fenced files was left as found; `packages/plugin-detail/src/RelatedList.tsx` (held by objectui#9050) was read but not touched.
